title: Bazaine and Castelnau → Napoleon III, Mexico, French cipher cable of 373 cable words intercepted by Sheridan's telegrapher Charles A. Keefer, never deciphered
correspondents: Marshal François-Achille Bazaine and General Castelnau → Napoleon III (copy sent by Charles A. Keefer → Gen. U. S. Grant)
place: Mexico City (transmitted via the French consulate, New Orleans)
shelfmark: Keefer to Grant, New Orleans, 17 Dec 1866, William H. Seward Papers (University of Rochester), Library of Congress microcopy roll 98 (Weber, Masked Dispatches ch. 17 nn. 46, 60)
folio_note: 373 cable words of a French numeric code (groups like 2209 613 562 273 15 2214, Weber n. 46) copied by Keefer from the line; plain text of the same message printed by Georges Girard, La vie et les souvenirs du général Castelnau (Paris 1930), pp. 117-118
status: Weber (Masked Dispatches, 3rd ed. 2013, pp. 114-116 and n. 63): Keefer 'could not decipher it' and hoped for the plain text from a French newspaper; 'There is no evidence Keefer ever solved the French cipher.' The plain text was published in 1930, so the content is known; the French cipher system itself was never reconstructed. Not in the repo (known.py: Keefer, Bazaine no hits).
why: A rare surviving ciphertext of the French numeric diplomatic/army code at the end of the Mexican intervention, with a published plaintext: a known-plaintext rebuild of part of the code that could then read Keefer's other French intercepts of Dec 1866.

verify: Locate Keefer's 17 Dec 1866 letter (Seward Papers reel 98; check whether Papers of Ulysses S. Grant vol. 16 prints the cipher); get Girard 1930 pp. 117-118 for the plaintext; align.

title: German Foreign Office → Bernstorff (Washington), German cipher telegram forwarded through the US Embassy Berlin (Grew), text not printed in FRUS
correspondents: German Foreign Office → Count Bernstorff, German ambassador at Washington (via Chargé Joseph C. Grew → Secretary of State)
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, 1910-29 decimal file (World War I series; FRUS 1916 Supplement doc. 424)
folio_note: FRUS prints only Grew's covering telegram: '[German cipher. Not printed.]'. The file copy, 841.857/244, M580 roll 191 frame 0111, reads '(Quote German cipher)' and has no groups.
status: FRUS 1916 Supplement, The World War, doc. 424: Grew forwards 'the following cipher telegram which is said to relate to' the Washington talks; the German code text is omitted. German diplomatic traffic sent over the US channel in 1916-17 was in codes 13040/0075 and was largely read by Room 40, so a decrypt may exist in TNA (HW 7, ADM 223); not checked. 2 Nov 2026 (targets/bernstorff1917/, section 10): the file copy, 841.857/244, keeps no groups; the cipher was delivered to the Ambassador on 7 Dec 1916. The telegram concerns the Arabia case. No ciphertext is known, so this entry is no crib for catalogue 657. 6 Nov 2026 (targets/arabia1916/): M580-191 frames 0109-0113 viewed, no German groups; FRUS, Bernstorff 1920 searched; closed as attempted, open (arabia1916.html).
why: German code text passed by the State Department during the 1916 peace-note period; checkable against the Room 40 codebooks reconstructed for 13040.

The NARA original is in Records of the Dept of State relating to internal affairs of Great Britain, microfilm M580 reel 191 (870 images); I viewed images 0090-0113 via the catalog IIIF URLs. Image 0111: Telegram Received, Green and German cipher, Berlin via Copenhagen, dated 5 Dec 1916, rec d 6 Dec 11.45 pm, stamped 841.857/244; text 4691, December 5, 6 p.m. Foreign Office requests me to transmit ... cipher telegram ... Quote. (Quote German cipher). End quote. GREW. EGAN. So the German cipher is not copied on the page. Neighbours: 0109 = /242 Dept of State to London; 0112 = /245 Havre consul; 0110 = ? ; 0102-0108 = Berlin 4685 (blue cipher, Dec 3-4), clear text.
frame_check.note: The embassy telegram carries only the placeholder (Quote German cipher); the German cipher text itself is absent from this file as filmed. Frame numbers are file image numbers of M580-191.

known: Grew's covering telegram 4691 read (FRUS 1916 Supp. 424; NARA M580-191-0111): 'Quote German cipher', no groups; frames 0109-0113 (841.857/242-246) show no German code sheet. Bernstorff's letter of 8 Dec 1916 (Lansing Papers I no. 547) paraphrases the instruction (settle the Marina and Arabia cases in Washington). Not in Bernstorff 1920 (arabia1916.html).
open: The telegram itself: the groups were delivered to the Ambassador on 7 Dec 1916 and never kept in the State Department file. Needs the Politisches Archiv draft or a Room 40 decrypt (TNA HW 7 / ADM 137); neither checked online.
access_note: not online: the NARA file copy and FRUS carry no groups; the German draft (PA AA Berlin) or a British decrypt (TNA) would have to be photographed.
